name: Kuo-Sheng Reactor Neutrino Laboratory
notes: Kind `reactor_site` (as for Daya Bay and Chooz): the laboratory is inside the reactor building at a nuclear power station, 28 m from the core; it is also a shallow underground laboratory (~30 m.w.e.), but the reactor is what defines it.
The neutrino-physics programme of TEXONO (neutrino-electron scattering, magnetic moment, CEvNS searches) shares this facility; the dark-matter stream records only the germanium dark-matter work.

operator_text.note: The source names the power station's operator; it does not say who operates the laboratory itself, which is run by the TEXONO Collaboration (led by Academia Sinica, Taipei).
operator_text.quote: The Kuo-Sheng Reactor Neutrino Laboratory (KSNL) is located at a distance of 28 m from the core #1 of the Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station operated by the Taiwan Power Company at the northern shore of Taiwan.
operator_text.value: Taiwan Power Company (operator of the Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station that hosts the laboratory)

summary.plain: A small physics laboratory built next to a reactor core inside the Kuo-Sheng nuclear power plant on the northern coast of Taiwan. Under about thirty metres of water-equivalent shielding from the building, it hosts the TEXONO germanium detectors used for reactor-neutrino and light dark matter searches.
summary.technical: Laboratory on the ground floor of the reactor building of the Kuo-Sheng Nuclear Power Station (2.9 GW thermal; Taiwan Power Company), 28 m from core #1, ~12 m below sea level with ~30 m.w.e. overburden; 4-pi passive shielding (5 cm Cu, 25 cm boron-loaded polyethylene, 5 cm steel, 15 cm Pb) plus cosmic-ray veto panels. First physics data July 2001. The power station was decommissioned in March 2023.
